data.narrative:
Cortical Labs is a Series A AI & Software company founded by Hon Weng Chong and Andy Kitchen that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 5 private companies at Series A and Series B stages, including Scale AI ($29.0B), Reflection AI ($25.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), and Field AI ($2.0B), alongside one public comparable (Palantir).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $11M raised proxy, yielding $22M. The peer-median method benchmarks against the five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, which exhibit a median valuation of $5.6B with a range of $2.0B to $29.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneous investor sentiment and stage variance within the AI frontier-tech sector.

Synthesizing both methods produces a low bound of $19M, median of $2.8B, and high bound of $6.4B. The stage-progression result sits well below peer medians, reflecting Cortical's earlier capital deployment. Key uncertainties include revenue traction and technological differentiation relative to the peer cohort, particularly given the 14.5x gap between low and median estimates. The peer-median approach dominates the analysis given data limitations, but the wide peer range ($2.0B–$29.0B) underscores sector-level valuation volatility and the materiality of company-specific factors in pricing.
